gen-dafont-hammerhead-newsreader: Stark and ruler-straight, Hammerhead lays down an outline with no swelling anywhere, while Newsreader underneath lets its strokes thicken and thin just slightly. That quiet stroke variation is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-source-serif-4: Authoritative from the first glance. Hammerhead keeps every stroke at one gauge, and Source Serif 4 tightens gently at the curve tops, so the difference in stroke contrast is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-hero-fs-hind: Hind reads with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals and curves that never turn inward on themselves. And Hero, if shrunk down, would see its closed, widely spaced letters lose that long sweep.
gen-dafont-highway-gothic-fs-bespoke-ser: Highway Gothic packs its glyphs tightly like a stack of cut sheets, with an open c and strokes of constant width. But Bespoke Serif does the opposite job, thin strokes at half the weight of thick ones lending a dignified, classic serif finish.
gen-dafont-hiruko-fs-bespoke-serif: Bespoke Serif brings thick and thin strokes in a dignified rhythm. Hiruko holds a pen that never shifts pressure, and that unvarying line against a serif's modulation is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-impact-label-lora: Lora reads as bookish and warm, its c opening broad and its hairlines thinning only modestly at the curves. And Impact Label stands over it with a high-set x-height and letters sitting apart like beads, heavy against Lora's moderate lowercase.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-gambetta: Jelly Crazies has bowls that nearly seal shut. Beneath it, Gambetta's wide channels into each counter and gently shifting stroke weight let a text serif move along at an easy, graceful clip.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-noto-serif: Playful heading, studious body. Jelly Crazies has no thinning at all, while Noto Serif swings mellowly from thick to thin, and its prominent x-height can stay at a modest size without losing presence.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-gambetta: Joystix is all widely tracked arcade lettering, its stems barely heavier than their arms and its x-height crowding the ascender line. And Gambetta, with moderate lowercase and a serif's graceful weight shifts, gives that blocky look somewhere softer to land.
gen-dafont-joystix-lora: Chunky, widely tracked arcade lettering with stems only a shade heavier than its arms, set above Lora's broad-mouthed curves and modest hairlines. The classic serif below brings a lower, literary lowercase to settle it.
